ideas.pitch: An offline-first, LoRa-based peer-to-peer messaging and data relay protocol designed to reconstitute community communication networks after a total collapse of cellular and internet infrastructure.
ideas.title: AetherMesh
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly aligns with the core 'Day Zero' civilization-rebuilding mission by focusing on foundational communication infrastructure, and its focus on a live, demonstrable local mesh network mirrors the winning pattern of a working prototype.

ideas.pitch: A low-power IoT monitoring dashboard and load-balancing simulator for off-grid micro-hydro and human-powered generators in a resource-scarce post-collapse settlement.
ideas.title: KinetiGrid
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the winning pattern of clear, measurable impact by tracking energy consumption metrics and resource longevity, appealing directly to judges looking for practical engineering and long-term scalability.

ideas.pitch: An offline-capable AI clinical assistant and herbal-remedy database that helps survivors triage injuries, identify safe local flora, and manage basic healthcare when modern hospitals vanish.
ideas.title: AegisBio
ideas.why_it_could_win: Adopts the proven execution strategy of SAGACITY by bringing essential healthcare knowledge to low-connectivity, high-need environments, scoring high on practical utility for survival.

ideas.pitch: A decentralized ledger and physical barcode allocation system for tracking, rationing, and sharing community seed banks, grain reserves, and potable water supplies.
ideas.title: SiloVault
ideas.why_it_could_win: Tackles societal resilience and asset management with a functional inventory dashboard, following the exact success pattern of JalSetu at the Smart India Hackathon.

ideas.pitch: An open-source water purification monitoring and community task-allocation platform to prevent waterborne disease outbreaks in early-stage rebuilt settlements.
ideas.title: TerraSan
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines environmental monitoring with community governance, fulfilling the requirement for practical engineering and long-term societal scalability.
